claim: The Constitution is the one authority on whether an act may happen: the old governance and security modules are gone and nothing reaches them, and every capability absorbed from them works where it now lives.
hypothesis: If the collapse is real, no file imports a deleted module, only the Constitution writes containment events or reads the declared policy, and each absorbed capability refuses what its old owner refused while passing what it passed.

checks.label: no deleted module can be imported
nothing imports a deleted module (core, tests, experiments, repo root)
the tool gate puts every act to the Constitution
nothing in front of the gate refuses: no isolation check, no second gate
checks.detail: only the recovery THROTTLE delay precedes it

checks.label: the gate does not hand the Constitution what a tool says about itself
recovery isolation is gone, comments included
checks.detail: no ISOLATE action, no isolation state, no mention

checks.label: one writer of containment events (halt, resume, quarantine, release)
one integrity detector (the Constitution's baseline)
one reader of the declared policy file
tools declare no consequence — the slot is gone from the tool base class
the substrate measures consequence itself (no tool declaration, no trigger engine)
checks.detail: classify_action reads the tool name and its arguments only

checks.label: the tool domain reads the substrate's measurement
no deleting command is read as inspection or allowed
ordinary reads still pass
the policy loads as target rules, act rules and rules no act can carry
data egress is refused on principle
chaos testing against production is refused
fuzzing with code execution is refused
chaos aimed at its own governance needs a human, so is refused
their benign variants are not refused on principle (only sent back: nothing proves them)
a declared consequence raises the measured one, never lowers it
the baseline hashes the declared policy file
a change to it is caught as CRITICAL
the file was restored byte-identical
checks.detail: sha256 matches; no finding after restore

checks.label: a newer row the Constitution did not write does not hide its halt
and its own resume does lift it
it covers what judging reads (the Constitution, intent, ThreatSense)
and nothing in it is unprotected
a directive telling the substrate to set aside its governance is refused
an ordinary directive is allowed
the security check reads the self-defense surface
health no longer probes deleted modules

notes: Static checks parse every file; live checks judge real acts through a real Constitution and never execute them. The declared policy file is modified for one check and restored byte-identical (sha256 re-checked).
